title: Circulatory System
cheat_card: Circulatory systems move fluid through the body, either open (hemolymph in hemocoel cavity) or closed (blood in vessels). Arteries carry blood away under high pressure; veins return blood under low pressure and contain valves to prevent backflow.

Path of Blood (Human): Right atrium → tricuspid valve → right ventricle → pulmonary semilunar valve → pulmonary arteries (lungs) → pulmonary veins → left atrium → bicuspid (mitral) valve → left ventricle → aortic semilunar valve → aorta → systemic circuit.

Heartbeat Control: Sinoatrial (SA) node acts as the pacemaker to initiate electrical signals; Atrioventricular (AV) node delays and transmits signals to the ventricles to coordinate contraction (systole = contraction, diastole = relaxation).

ECG Waves: P wave represents atrial depolarization (about to contract); QRS complex represents ventricular depolarization (about to contract, atria relaxing); T wave represents ventricular repolarization (recovery).
memory_anchor:
Heart Valve Position Mnemonic

Remember: Try before you Buy

  • Tricuspid valve is on the Right side of the heart.
  • Bicuspid (mitral) valve is on the Left side of the heart.

flashcards.q: Trace the pathway of a red blood cell from the systemic tissues back to the systemic tissues in a human.
flashcards.a: Systemic tissues -> Venae cavae -> Right atrium -> Tricuspid valve -> Right ventricle -> Pulmonary semilunar valve -> Pulmonary trunk/arteries -> Lungs (oxygenation) -> Pulmonary veins -> Left atrium -> Bicuspid (mitral) valve -> Left ventricle -> Aortic semilunar valve -> Aorta -> Systemic arteries/tissues.

flashcards.q: What are the events corresponding to the P, QRS, and T waves of an electrocardiogram (ECG)?
flashcards.a: The P wave represents atrial depolarization (atria about to contract, triggered by the SA node); the QRS complex represents ventricular depolarization (ventricles about to contract) and hides atrial repolarization; the T wave represents ventricular repolarization (ventricular recovery).

flashcards.q: Explain how blood is returned to the heart in low-pressure veins against gravity.
flashcards.a: Venous return is driven by skeletal muscle contraction (which squeezes the veins and pushes blood forward), one-way valves (which prevent backflow), and a respiratory pump (which decreases thoracic pressure during inspiration, pulling blood into the chest cavity).

outline_blanks: The mammalian heart features a double-loop pathway. Deoxygenated blood enters the [[right atrium]] via the venae cavae, passes through the [[tricuspid]] valve, and is pumped to the lungs, while oxygenated blood is pumped by the thick-walled [[left ventricle]] into the [[aorta]]. Heart rhythm is coordinated by the [[sinoatrial node]] pacemaker.
